notes: Heritage sign recovery for a listed 1911 building: the house crest survives ONLY on a weathered engraved-brass entry plaque (late-afternoon raking light throws a specular bevel ridge brighter than the engraved field so it traces as if it were geometry, and along the shaded left third the incised line and the brass run to one value so the wreath simply drops out there) and on a SMALL crest inside a BIG 1950s letterhead scan (printed small, the ink gained until the two interior keystone rules merged into one bar and the ribbon banner's counters filled solid — a closure invisible on the sheet, obvious only beside the plaque trace at suite-plate size). Plus a facade approval frame where the shaded limestone reveal and the brass plaque field share a tonal value along the plaque's left edge so an automatic isolation reports success, previews cleanly and bites a crescent of the old engraving with a ragged stone boundary at full res; the 2019 shop's single-ink NO-BLEED plate PDF whose suite number and firm name look like two blocks but are one continuous text story reached by position, still carrying the abandoned '3C' numbering in its own text; a 16-row schedule that is really 14 suites (two renumbered suites doubled old-number+new-number, one vacant suite with an empty firm cell that would print a plate with a blank line, three ampersand firm names and one that runs to 38 characters) which must reconcile to 14 in board order; and the fabricator's clean survey pinning the physical panel sizes, substrates, fixings, fixing-clearance zones and the 0.50 mm minimum engraved stroke the 32 mm suite-plate crest is the tightest test of.

assets.defect_engineered: Raking-light specular ridge on the polished bevel reads BRIGHTER than the recessed engraved field so a level/threshold selection takes the ridge as if it were part of the crest; along the SHADED LEFT THIRD the incised line and the brass run to almost the same value so the laurel wreath gives no separation and does not come back there at all. Neither shows on the photo, which reads as the sharper, more authoritative source. (Carries checkpoint CP1, plaque half.)
assets.prompt: Photorealistic close handheld smartphone photograph of a weathered engraved cast-brass building name plaque mounted flush on a limestone facade, shot in late-afternoon raking sunlight coming from the RIGHT so the polished chamfered bevel around the plaque edge throws a bright specular ridge that reads noticeably BRIGHTER than the recessed engraved field, while the LEFT THIRD of the plaque falls into soft shadow where the incised engraved lines and the surrounding brass run to almost exactly the same tonal value and the engraving there nearly disappears into the metal. Engraved into the brass is an invented heritage house crest: a slender oval laurel wreath encircling a small stylised classical building keystone device that has two fine parallel horizontal interior rules cut across it, and beneath the wreath a narrow engraved ribbon banner bearing the small-caps roman numeral date MCMXI; below the crest, engraved capitals read THE MARCHFIELD EXCHANGE. Real brass patina, fine tarnish, small surface scratches, genuine incised V-groove engraving catching the low sun, the crest filling most of the frame, casual real-world snapshot, not a studio shot. Entirely invented fictional crest and building name, no real logos, no real trademarks, no real brand.

assets.defect_engineered: Printed small, the ink GAINED: the keystone device's two fine parallel interior rules have run together into a single thick bar and the ribbon banner's counters have filled solid, a closure invisible on the sheet and obvious only beside the plaque trace at suite-plate size. The crest occupies only a small part of a large scan, so a high-resolution-looking file is really a small source in a big file and nothing downstream may enlarge it. (Carries checkpoint CP1, letterhead half.)
assets.prompt: Flatbed scanner capture of an aged 1950s business letterhead sheet, one deep charcoal ink printed on cream laid stock, the sheet foxed and lightly browned at the edges, with a great deal of empty cream paper around a SMALL printed house crest sitting near the top centre at roughly thirty millimetres across so it occupies only a small part of the large scanned sheet. The crest is an invented heritage mark: a slender oval laurel wreath encircling a small stylised classical building keystone device, with a narrow ribbon banner beneath bearing the small-caps roman numeral date MCMXI, and under it the printed capitals THE MARCHFIELD EXCHANGE with a period address line in small serif type. Critically, because it was printed small the ink has GAINED: the two fine parallel horizontal interior rules across the keystone device have run together into a SINGLE thick solid bar with no gap between them, and the small counters inside the ribbon banner have FILLED SOLID with ink so those interior openings are lost. Even, flat, front-lit scan, no glare, subtle paper grain, foxing spots at the margins. Entirely invented fictional crest and brand, no real logos, no real trademarks.

assets.defect_engineered: In the shaded stone reveal the pale limestone surround and the tarnished brass plaque field run to almost the same value ALONG THE LEFT EDGE, so an automatic isolation of the plaque area reports success, previews convincingly at check scale and bites that edge, leaving a crescent of the old engraving inside the supposedly cleared field and a ragged stone boundary that only shows at full resolution. (Carries checkpoint CP3.)
assets.prompt: Photorealistic architectural photograph of the entrance bay of a listed 1911 stone commercial building, a recessed limestone door reveal in soft open shade, with the original weathered brass name plaque mounted flush on the limestone within the shaded reveal. The light in the reveal is even and nearly shadowless so that ALONG THE LEFT EDGE of the plaque the pale limestone surround and the tarnished brass plaque field run to almost exactly the same tonal value and the boundary between stone and brass nearly vanishes there, while the plaque's right edge separates more clearly from the stone. Carved stone surround, subtle weathering and faint lichen, a brass letter-slot and a small period lantern to one side, quiet dignified heritage entrance, shot straight on and framed generously for a board approval mockup showing the whole bay. Entirely invented fictional building, no legible signage text, no real logos, no real trademarks.

assets.content:
LAYOUT SPEC for the previous sign shop's single suite-plate press PDF (flat, single record; to be reverse-engineered into a live merge template downstream).

Document: single suite plate, 200 x 75 mm LANDSCAPE, NO bleed box present (trim = media box, 0 mm bleed), fonts embedded. One ink only, an engraving proof in Slate Ink #2C3439 on a white proof ground. This is the ONLY file the 2019 sign shop left; it is the artwork for ONE plate from that refit.

WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE PRINTED (two apparent blocks):
- Left: a small engraved house-crest lockup about 32 mm across, the 2019 shop's OWN redrawn tracing of the crest (decorative here; NOT to be reused as the recovered master).
- Right, upper: the SUITE NUMBER in a large bold serif, reads as its own block.
- Right, lower: the FIRM NAME in a smaller roman beneath it, reads as a second separate block.

HOW IT IS ACTUALLY SET (the reverse-engineering trap):
- The SUITE NUMBER and the FIRM NAME are a SINGLE continuous text story in ONE text frame (suite number, a forced line break, then the firm name), NOT two addressable frames. Downstream they can only be reached by position inside that one story, paragraph by paragraph, not frame by frame.
- The crest at left is a GROUP OF VECTOR PATHS (the 2019 shop's own tracing), NOT a rectangular picture/graphic frame; there is no image well anywhere on the plate to bind a recovered crest into.
- The sample plate carries the ABANDONED 2019 NUMBERING in its own text: it reads 'SUITE 3C' with the firm 'Corliss & Vane Solicitors'. 3C is a 2019 number the current schedule renumbered to 302, so the template's own baked text no longer matches the schedule and must be REPLACED, not trusted.

NO BLEED: because the media box equals the trim and no bleed box exists, a press-ready-with-bleed delivery cannot be honoured from anything derived from this file, however the render is called.

FIELD LABELS the downstream mapping must resolve (present as content, not visible tokens): SUITE_NUMBER | FIRM_NAME

Colours: white proof ground, Slate Ink #2C3439 single engraving ink; the crest device drawn in the same single ink.

assets.content:
THE MARCHFIELD EXCHANGE — SIGN PROGRAMME SITE SURVEY
Prepared by: Halloran Brass & Engraving Co. (fabricator)
Surveyed on site: front elevation and ground-floor lobby.

MACHINE / PROCESS
Rotary and V-groove engraving into solid brass, satin finish, wax-filled lines. We engrave from vector geometry, not from a picture: a filled shape with the pattern painted on it is no use on the machine.
MINIMUM ENGRAVED STROKE WIDTH WE CAN HOLD AT FINAL SIZE: 0.50 mm. Any line finer than 0.50 mm at the size it is actually engraved will not cut cleanly and will either drop out or fill. This is the hard limit for the whole programme.

1. ENTRANCE PLAQUE (replaces the existing plaque)
   Size: 450 x 300 mm, landscape.
   Substrate: 6 mm solid cast brass, satin finish, wax-filled engraving.
   Fixing: 4 x M8 countersunk brass bolts into the limestone, one near each corner. Keep all artwork at least 15 mm clear of each bolt centre.
   Crest engraved at 180 mm across at the head; THE MARCHFIELD EXCHANGE engraved beneath in capitals.

2. DIRECTORY BOARD (lobby, replaces the plastic board)
   Size: 600 x 900 mm, portrait.
   Substrate: engraved brass face on an oak backing panel, satin finish.
   Fixing: concealed cleat brackets, top edge 1600 mm above finished floor. 20 mm clear margin all round; nothing in the outer 20 mm.
   Crest engraved at 120 mm across at the head; the tenant lines beneath in suite order.

3. SUITE PLATES (one per suite)
   Size: 200 x 75 mm, landscape.
   Substrate: 3 mm solid brass, satin finish, wax-filled engraving.
   Fixing: 2 concealed studs plus adhesive, no visible fixings on the face. 12 mm clear margin all round.
   Layout: crest engraved at 32 mm across at the left; suite number and firm name engraved to the right.
   NOTE: at 32 mm the crest's finest interior lines are the tightest test of the 0.50 mm minimum on the whole job. Check them here first before anything is committed.

GENERAL
- All panels are satin brass, so proofs must be judged on brass, not on white.
- We will quote per panel from your schedule. Tell us up front any line you already know falls under 0.50 mm at its final size so we can flag it rather than cut it.
